attempts.summary: Configured node1 (VyOS) as a router between lan-a (node2, eth1/10.50.50.0/24) and lan-b (node3, eth2/10.60.60.0/24). Assigned node1's eth1=10.50.50.254 and eth2=10.60.60.254, saved config. Assigned persistent static IPs to node2's ens7 (10.50.50.11) and node3's ens7 (10.60.60.12) via /etc/network/interfaces.d/60-lan.cfg, each with a persistent route to the peer subnet via node1. ip_forward was already 1 on node1 and no firewall filters exist, so forwarding is unrestricted with no NAT (source addresses preserved). Verified bidirectional ping and TCP connectivity (via nc) with tcpdump confirming original source IPs (10.50.50.11 / 10.60.60.12) reach the peer unmodified. Then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all three nodes: captured boot_id baselines, restarted each node via native reboot, confirmed boot_id changed post-restart, and re-verified interface config, routes, and end-to-end connectivity (including source-IP-preserving TCP flow) after all three restarts completed.
